prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer stands facing forward and looking straight down at a floor (~1.0–1.5 m below the camera), with no other people present in the scene. The wearer's right arm (brightest white, ~0.2–0.7 m from the camera) and left arm (~0.3–0.8 m) extend from the bottom edge into the scene above their seated or standing legs (~0.6–1.2 m), surrounded by floor-level objects within arm's reach: an open rectangular container of dark hardware/fasteners straight ahead (~0.8–1.0 m), yellow and white wire coils ~0.2–0.3 m to its left, a small grey box beneath the left hand (~0.8 m), stacked cardboard boxes to the lower left (~1.1–1.4 m), and red tools and buckets to the right (~1.0–1.3 m). Across frames 1 to 4, the right hand reaches down into the container (~0.8 m away, partially occluding its interior and the yellow coil beneath it) while the left hand rests near the lower grey box, and in frame 5 both hands rise closer to the camera (~0.4–0.5 m) and meet centrally to hold a handful of fasteners above the container. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the vertical height of the elevated arms, knees, and tall container rims from the flat floor background and highlights the upward retraction of both hands toward the camera in frame 5. However, the depth map is unreliable between the wearer's legs (producing a pitch-black void artifact), across the upper-right wall/floor corner in frames 1 and 5 where brightness shifts inconsistently, and inside the dark container where individual fasteners are flattened into a single smooth surface.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates regions of the camera wearer's extended limbs in the foreground (~0.2–1.2 m from the camera) against an unsegmented black background, with no other people present and the wearer facing downward toward the floor. Across frames 1 to 4, it segments the right arm on the right (~0.2–0.8 m away, reaching into the upper container) and the left arm and legs on the left (~0.3–1.2 m away, separated by ~0.2–0.4 m laterally) as separate 'person' instances, before both hands converge in the center at ~0.4–0.5 m depth in frame 5. The map provides sharp silhouettes for the wearer's arms that stand out more clearly than in the cluttered RGB floor scene, and in frames 4 and 5 it delineates the boundary of the open fastener container (~0.8–1.0 m ahead) and a small round bucket to the right (~1.1 m away, ~0.3 m right of the container). However, the map is highly unreliable in class labeling and completeness: it splits the single camera wearer into multiple fragmented 'person' masks that bleed onto the floor and coiled wires in frames 1, 2, and 4, and completely misses the wire coils, tools, and cardboard boxes on the left. Furthermore, it misclassifies the fastener container as a 'book' in frame 4 and a 'cell phone' in frame 5, a small white bucket on the right as a 'cup' in frame 5, and a corner of a cardboard box at the bottom-left (~1.3 m away) as a 'remote' in frames 2 and 3.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only two magenta 2D hand skeletons on a black background, as the camera wearer's torso and head are behind the egocentric viewpoint and no other people are in the scene. In frames 1 to 4, both hands remain within arm's reach (~0.4–0.8 m from the camera and ~0.3–0.4 m apart vertically in the image plane), with the right hand positioned higher and slightly right inside the fastener container (~0.8 m deep) and the left hand positioned lower and to the left (~0.6–0.7 m deep) resting atop the grey box. Between frames 1 and 4, the right hand's finger keypoints curl inward from an open splay (frames 1–3) into a closed pinch (frame 4) as it grasps a cluster of fasteners, while the left hand remains stationary in a curled posture. In frame 5, both hands move toward each other and upward toward the camera (~0.4–0.5 m away), converging in the middle of the frame with their fingers curling around the transferred fasteners from opposite sides. This skeletal representation makes exact finger articulation, thumb opposition, and the transition from open reaching to pinching much easier to read than in the dark interior of the container in the RGB strip, though it is completely unreliable for tracking the wearer's visible legs and forearms (which lack yellow body skeletons) and suffers from self-occlusion where the fingers overlap the fasteners in frames 4 and 5.
